papers.title_in_file: Quantum Graph Attention Network: A Novel Quantum Multi-Head Attention Mechanism for Graph Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, related work, method, evaluation (4.1 to 4.3), conclusion; appendix not read.
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid graph neural network that computes attention coefficients with a variational quantum circuit, benchmarked against GAT and GATv2.

assertions.value: The authors report that QGAT surpasses GATv2 by approximately +0.7% on Pubmed, +1.75% on ogbn-arxiv, and +1.47% on ogbn-products, with results evaluated over five independent runs.
quotes: It surpasses GATv2 by approximately +0.7% on Pubmed, +1.75% on ogbn-arxiv, and +1.47% on ogbn-products.
All reported results reflect test set performance, evaluated at the best validation checkpoint over five independent runs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; baselines are classical GAT and GATv2 only.
assertions.reader_inference: The Pubmed gain is smaller than the reported standard deviation of QGAT in Table 1, so it may not be distinguishable from run-to-run variation. How the quantum circuit was executed (simulator or hardware) is not stated in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors report that on ogbn-arxiv QGAT outperforms GAT and GATv2 at all tested levels of Gaussian feature noise and under added random edges.
assertions.anchor: Section 4.1 Robustness to Noise, Figure 2, p.7 (values are in the figure, not in the text)
quotes: While all models degrade with stronger perturbations, QGAT consistently outperforms GAT and GATv2 across all levels.
However, QGAT consistently outperforms both GAT and GATv2, maintaining a higher accuracy margin especially under moderate to severe noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one dataset; numbers only in Figure 2.
assertions.reader_inference: The attribution of robustness to amplitude encoding and entanglement is the authors' interpretation; no ablation is given in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors report that on ogbn-proteins QGAT attains a ROC-AUC of 79.41%, which they describe as competitive with GATv2 with lower variance, not as higher.
quotes: On ogbn-proteins, QGAT attains a ROC-AUC of 79.41%, performing competitively with GATv2 while exhibiting lower variance
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 2 lists GATv2 at a slightly higher ROC-AUC than QGAT here, which sits against the conclusion's wording that QGAT consistently outperforms the baselines.

assertions.value: The authors state that hardware scalability remains a key limitation, because the current implementation does not support distributed quantum-classical execution across multiple GPUs or nodes.
assertions.anchor: Section 5 Discussion and Future Work, p.9
quotes: However, hardware scalability remains a key limitation. Our current implementation does not support distributed quantum-classical execution across multiple GPUs or nodes
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit, Section 5, p.9.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Computing in Transport Science: A Review
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, problem formulation start, gate-based section 3.3, applications summary and Table 4, conclusion; detailed per-algorithm sections skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A review of gate-based quantum computing, quantum annealing and quantum machine learning applied to transportation problems.

assertions.value: The authors state that the review focuses on three paradigms: gate-based quantum computing, quantum annealing and quantum machine learning.
quotes: It focuses on three principal paradigms: Gate-based quantum computing, Quantum annealing, and Quantum machine learning
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that gate-based quantum computing is still at an early stage of technology maturity, with practical applications limited to small-scale quantum processors.
quotes: Currently, the gate-based QC is still in early stages of technology maturity, with practical applications limited to small-scale quantum processors.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review author's statement about the field with no single study behind it.

assertions.value: The authors state that efficient quantum algorithms for NP-Complete problems have yet to be discovered, and that the current limits on qubit number and decoherence errors restrict the practical use of gate-based systems on NP-complete problems.
quotes: However, it is important to note that efficient quantum algorithms for NP-Complete problems have yet to be discovered.
Furthermore, the current limitations in gate-based systems
assertions.certainty_reason: Statement about the state of the field from a review, not proved in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum annealing approaches have been highly successful in solving QUBO problems, in contrast with gate-based systems limited in their application to NP-complete problems.
quotes: Where gate-based systems have been limited in its application to NP-complete problems, QA approaches have been highly successful in solving QUBO problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review-level assertion; 'highly successful' is not defined or measured in the conclusion.
assertions.reader_inference: The sentence gives no benchmark or comparison against classical solvers, so it does not support a claim of quantum advantage.

papers.title_in_file: MerLin: A Discovery Engine for Photonic and Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, architecture overview, Section III reproduction summaries and Table I, Section IV discussion; code blocks and reference list not read in detail.
papers.what_it_is: An open-source photonic and hybrid QML framework from Quandela, with reproductions of eighteen published QML works.

assertions.value: The authors, at Quandela, describe MerLin as an open-source framework designed as a discovery engine for photonic and hybrid quantum machine learning, and state that they reproduce eighteen photonic and hybrid QML works with it.
quotes: We introduce MerLin, an open-source framework designed as a discovery engine for photonic and hybrid quantum machine learning.
we reproduce eighteen state-of-the-art photonic and hybrid QML works
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describing its own product.

assertions.value: The authors report that the MerLin implementation reproduced the original Perceval SSIM results while reducing training time by up to a factor of 15.
assertions.anchor: Section III-F Image generation / reproduction summary, p.4-5
quotes: The MerLin implementation reproduced the original Perceval SSIM results while reducing training time by up to a factor of 15.
assertions.certainty_reason: Vendor benchmark of its own software against its own earlier code (Perceval).
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is between two Quandela products, so it speaks to software speed, not to any quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors report that in one reproduction the original paper's up to 3.14% accuracy gain for a quantum-enhanced model was not found: the best quantum and classical models all reached approximately 89% accuracy with no clear separation.
assertions.anchor: Section III, summary of reproductions, p.4
quotes: Whereas the original paper reports up to a 3.14% accuracy gain for the quantum-enhanced model, our reproduction found that the best quantum and classical models all reached approximately 89% accuracy, with no clear separation between them.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single reproduction result reported in summary form.
assertions.reader_inference: A failed reproduction of a published quantum gain bears on how far single published QML accuracy gains can be trusted.

assertions.value: The authors state that their replication of quantum LLM fine-tuning on SST2 sentiment analysis used a binary classification setting that appears too simple to draw definitive conclusions about quantum utility.
assertions.anchor: Section III-G Benchmark tasks for model expressivity and robustness
quotes: we replicate the quantum LLM fine-tuning results from [39] on SST2 sentiment analysis; however, the binary classification setting appears too simple to draw definitive conclusions about quantum utility
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in Section III-G.

papers.title_in_file: Optimization Strategies for Variational Quantum Algorithms in Noisy Landscapes
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections II to VII (setup, landscapes, results), discussion and conclusion; Appendix A algorithm descriptions not read.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation benchmark of more than fifty metaheuristic optimizers for the variational quantum eigensolver under finite-shot sampling noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that, across models, CMA-ES and iL-SHADE consistently achieved the best performance for noisy VQE, that Simulated Annealing (Cauchy), Harmony Search and Symbiotic Organisms Search also showed robustness, and that PSO, GA and standard DE variants degraded sharply with noise.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Section VII, p.1 and p.30
quotes: Across models, CMA-ES and iL-SHADE consistently achieved the best performance, while Simulated Annealing (Cauchy), Harmony Search, and Symbiotic Organisms Search also showed robustness.
In contrast, widely used optimizers such as PSO, GA, and standard DE variants degraded sharply with noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study on Ising and Hubbard models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the benchmark used a three-phase procedure ending in a Hubbard model with 192 parameters, with Hubbard convergence tested at 5120 shots and at 64 shots, averaged over 5 independent runs.
assertions.anchor: Abstract; Section V, p.1 and p.11-12
quotes: the top-performing optimizers from the previous phases were analyzed on the Hubbard model with 192 parameters.
a high-shot scenario with 5120 shots and a low-shot scenario with 64 shots.
Convergence curves were plotted using the mean function evaluations over 5 independent runs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup, Section V.
assertions.reader_inference: All results are simulations with sampled noise; no run on quantum hardware is reported in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the landscape analysis explains the systematic failure of COBYLA and SPSA once noise is introduced, and motivates global sampling-based metaheuristics that do not depend on stable gradients.
quotes: These observations explain the systematic failure of COBYLA and SPSA once noise is introduced, and they motivate the use of global, sampling-based metaheuristics that do not depend on stable gradients.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result with an interpretation drawn from landscape plots in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that metaheuristic performance on noiseless benchmarks is not predictive of outcomes on noisy quantum simulations.
quotes: Taken together, our findings suggest that metaheuristic performance on noiseless benchmarks is not predictive of outcomes on noisy quantum simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical conclusion from one simulation study.
assertions.reader_inference: The point carries over to any claim of optimizer quality that was tested only with exact (noiseless) simulation.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for Predicting Anastomotic Leak: A Clinical Study
papers.version_note: The file's title differs from the filename ('Predicting Post-Surgical Complications with Quantum Neural Networks'); the content is the anastomotic leak QNN study the record names.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, noise-simulation section, QNN results and comparison discussion, sample-size discussion, conclusion and future-work list; statistical-methods and interpretability details skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulated-noise benchmark of quantum neural networks against tuned classical models for predicting anastomotic leak in a 200-patient clinical dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that among the QNN configurations the EfficientSU2-BFGS combination achieved the highest mean AUC, 0.7966, and RealAmplitudes with CMA-ES excelled in Average Precision, 0.5041.
quotes: The EfficientSU2-BFGS combination achieved the highest mean AUC of 0.7966
RealAmplitudes with CMA-ES excelled in Average Precision (0.5041
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small clinical dataset, simulated noise.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study used a clinical dataset of 200 patients with four key predictors and ZZFeatureMap encoding, with the circuits simulated under hardware noise models at 1024 shots per circuit execution, not run on quantum hardware.
assertions.anchor: Abstract p.1; Section V Simulating QNNs with noise
quotes: Using a clinical dataset of 200 patients and four key predictors identified through statistical analysis, we evaluated QNNs with ZZFeatureMap encoding
simulated under realistic hardware noise models
The simulation was configured to use 1024 shots per circuit execution
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the abstract and Section V.

assertions.value: The authors state that the primary limitation is the small sample size (N=200, with 28 AL events), that the results must be considered preliminary, and that validation on larger, independent, multi-center datasets is required before any clinical application.
assertions.anchor: Discussion on sample size, and Conclusion
quotes: the primary limitation of this study: the small sample size (N=200, with 28 AL events).

the results must be considered preliminary. The potential advantages of QNNs shown here require validation on larger, independent, multi-center datasets before any clinical application can be considered.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in the Discussion and Conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors report that at a fixed sensitivity of 83% their simulated QNNs show potential as powerful classification tools, while classical models, particularly the Multi-Layer Perceptron, excelled at probability calibration.
quotes: At a fixed, clinically crucial sensitivity of 83%, our results suggest that QNNs, simulated with realistic hardware noise, have the potential to be powerful classification tools
Conversely, classical models, particularly the Multi-Layer Perceptron, excelled at probability calibration
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small dataset; authors call it preliminary.
assertions.reader_inference: With only 28 leak events the QNN versus classical difference may not be distinguishable from chance.

papers.title_in_file: Threshold for Fault-tolerant Quantum Advantage with the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion and limitations, start of the appendix theorem; the circuit compilation and resource-count sections were skimmed, not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A fault-tolerant resource estimate for QAOA with amplitude amplification on random 8-SAT, giving the crossover point against classical heuristics.

assertions.value: The authors report a resource estimate in which QAOA with amplitude amplification at depth p = 623 crosses over with state-of-the-art classical heuristics at 179 variables and 14.99 hours of runtime on a surface-code fault-tolerant quantum computer with 73.91 million physical qubits.
quotes: with QAOA depth p = 623, QAOA+AA achieves a crossover with state-of-the-art classical heuristics at 179 variables and 14.99 hours of runtime
when executed on a surface-code-based fault-tolerant quantum computer with 73.91 million physical qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Resource estimate resting on an extrapolated scaling law from another paper and on stated hardware assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: The estimate is for one problem family (random 8-SAT) at 73.91 million physical qubits, far beyond any current device.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study focuses on the random 8-SAT problem and that validating the estimated speedups on hard industrially-relevant optimization problems is a future direction.
assertions.anchor: Section I and Section III Discussion
quotes: In this work, we focus on the random 8-SAT problem
validating that the speedups we estimate also hold for hard industrially-relevant optimization problems
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Section I and the Discussion.

assertions.value: The authors state two major limitations: they rely on the power-law decay of the asymptotic quantum scaling exponent with QAOA depth reported in an earlier work, whose evidence is for small depths and may not persist, and they do not consider the cost of routing qubits.
quotes: First, we rely on the power-law decay of the asymptotic quantum scaling exponent with QAOA depth p, reported in Ref. [1].
may not persist as p grows
Second, we do not consider the cost of routing qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits in Section III, p.9.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classical Sparrow solver is parallelized under an energy budget equal to that of surface-code decoding, which at the main crossover is 46 CPU cores with a power budget of 269.27 W.
quotes: we require that the total energy consumption of the CPUs running Sparrow is equal to that required to perform real-time decoding of the surface code
which is equal to that of state-of-the-art classical solver running on 46 CPU cores with a power budget of 269.27 W.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own comparison setup in Section I.
assertions.reader_inference: The crossover depends on this energy-matching choice; the abstract notes it can be relaxed, which changes the crossover time.

papers.title_in_file: Analog Quantum Feature Selection with Neutral-Atom Quantum Processors
papers.partial_detail: Whole body read: abstract, introduction, method, embedding, evaluation, results, conclusions. Fig. 5 and Table II values are in tables and figures and are not quoted.
papers.what_it_is: A feature selection method that maps mutual information to a Rydberg atom array Hamiltonian, tested in simulation on three tabular classification datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that, compared with mutual information ranking and Boruta combined with XGBoost and Random Forest classifiers, their quantum approach achieves competitive or superior performance, with a consistent advantage when selecting small feature subsets.
assertions.anchor: Abstract p.1; Section VII Conclusions p.6
quotes: Compared to classical methods such as mutual information ranking and Boruta, combined with XGBoost and Random Forest classifiers, our quantum-computing approach achieves competitive or superior performance.
QFS shows a consistent advantage when selecting small subsets
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulation on three datasets; the authors include a company (Kipu Quantum).
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against two classical selectors only; Table II shows ranking beating QFS on some precision or recall cells.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation is a noise-free simulation with the Amazon Braket analog Hamiltonian simulation environment, not a run on physical Rydberg hardware.
quotes: Overall, this simulation framework provides a hardware-aligned and noise-free evaluation of the protocol's performance
While the current implementation relies on simulation using Amazon Braket's ahs environment
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation-only setup in Sections IV-B and VII.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation uses three public binary classification datasets (Adult Income, Bank Marketing, Telco Churn) and covers problems with up to 20 features.
quotes: The proposed analog QFS framework was evaluated on three publicly available binary classification datasets
although this study focuses on problems with up to 20 features
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Sections V-A and VII.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the analog quantum model supports a natural encoding of larger feature spaces by expanding the atomic array, and that the framework is inherently scalable; no experiment at that scale is reported.
quotes: The analog quantum model supports a natural encoding of larger feature spaces by expanding the atomic array
the QFS framework is inherently scalable
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim without evidence in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Solving Drone Routing Problems with Quantum Computing: A Hybrid Approach Combining Quantum Annealing and Gate-Based Paradigms
papers.partial_detail: Whole body read: abstract, introduction, background, method, use cases, conclusions.
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid drone routing method using QAOA for clustering and D-Wave quantum annealing for routing, run on three use cases.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method is divided into two phases: a clustering phase executed with QAOA, and a routing phase that uses quantum annealers.
quotes: The algorithm is divided into two different phases: an initial clustering phase executed using a Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), and a routing phase employing quantum annealers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own method design in the abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the first use case, with instances of 12, 16 and 22 visiting points, the routes from their method were assessed against Google OR-Tools solutions and both methods yielded identical results in all examined cases.
quotes: Each case has been tested on three distinct instances, consisting of 12, 16, and 22 visiting points, respectively.
In all examined cases, both methods yielded identical results, thereby demonstrating the reliability of the system developed in this paper.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on small self-generated instances.
assertions.reader_inference: Matching a classical solver on 12 to 22 points shows correctness, not quantum advantage; no timing or cost comparison is quoted.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the third use case it has not been possible to compare with a classical method, and that this comparison is left as future work.
assertions.anchor: Section IV, end of use case 3
quotes: Due to the unique characteristics of this use case, it has not been possible to conduct a comparison with a classical method, as done for the previous use cases.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the current constraints of quantum hardware, including the limited number of qubits and decoherence and noise, limit the size and complexity of problems that can be efficiently addressed.
assertions.anchor: Section V Conclusions and Further Work
quotes: The current constraints of quantum hardware, including the limited number of qubits and issues related to decoherence and noise, limit the size and complexity of problems that can be efficiently addressed.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in Section V.
